statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the following holds: for every i64 value x, x occurs in r if and only if 0 <= x <= n and S(x) = M; and no value occurs more than once in r. Here x occurs in r means there exists k with 0 <= k < len(r) and r[k] = x. Equivalently, r contains exactly all division indices whose division score is the maximum M, in any order and without duplicates.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every j with 0 <= j < n, nums[j] is either 0 or 1. For each integer i with 0 <= i <= n define S(i) = (number of j with 0 <= j < i and nums[j] = 0) + (number of j with i <= j < n and nums[j] = 1), and let M = max_{0 <= k <= n} S(k).

statement: For every valid input, the function returns a result r; it does not fail by overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and, for every j with 0 <= j < n, nums[j] is either 0 or 1.
